definition: In coaching, directive refers to a more guiding style in which the coach takes a more active role in shaping the conversation and steering progress toward goals, rather than mainly drawing solutions from the coachee. In the source, it is used as the opposite of a non-directive approach.

reasons: The packet supports that directive coaching is contrasted with non-directive coaching, but it does not define directive as a more guiding style or say the coach actively shapes the conversation and steers progress toward goals.
The claim that directive coaching works by drawing less from the coachee’s own solutions is not stated in the packet and is an unsupported generalization.

The packet does not define “directive” as “a guiding style” where the coach “takes a more active role in shaping the conversation and steering progress toward goals”; it only references “directive versus non-directive coaching styles” and that AI versions were developed using Heron’s intervention analysis model.

The packet does not explicitly state that “directive” is the opposite of a “non-directive approach,” even though it contrasts the two styles; that explicit definitional relationship is not provided as a clear definition.
The definition attributes “mainly drawing solutions from the coachee” to the non-directive style; the packet does not provide this characterization.
